transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here because... lately, every time I have to get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or really any kind of upper platform for work, my head just tells me I'm about to go over. 

It's getting really bad. Even when I can look right at it and see the rails are in place, and I know the setup is supposed to be totally safe... I just can't shake it.
Does this intense fear only happen when you're actually facing heights like scaffolds or roof edges, or do you also get sudden waves of panic in other situations that have nothing to do with heights?

No, it's really just the heights. I don't get those waves of panic out of nowhere or in other situations. If I'm on the ground level, I'm completely fine. It only hits me when I'm actually facing a drop or having to go up on a structure.
